title: What If the Dinosaur-Killing Asteroid Hit Earth Today?

scenes.text: What if the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs hit today? The worst part isn't the blast.
It released energy equal to about 10 billion Hiroshima bombs, and ignited fires thousands of miles away.
Within a day, a tsunami swept out from the crater, then rushed back. About 130 meters of debris piled in.
The impact threw up sulfur, around 325 billion tons of it, blocking the sunlight.
Surface temperatures fell by as much as 26 degrees Celsius, and stayed below freezing for over three years.
In the end, 76 percent of all species died. The cold killed more than the blast.

description:
What if the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs hit again today?
Researchers estimate the impact released energy equal to 10 billion atomic bombs, but the lasting damage was the cold.
